findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not migrated to the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `init` returns immediately when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` already exists. Realms that already enabled ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 before this change therefore never get the newly added `Clients` resource or the new scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`). On such realms, creating a `Clients` scope permission later fails in `getOrCreateResource` because `scopeStore.findByName` returns null for the new scopes and throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")`. Code paths that look up the `Clients` all-resource also receive null. `init` must reconcile an existing admin-permissions client with the current schema instead of only creating it when absent.

findings.title: Per-client resources hide global all-clients permissions
findings.body: `hasPermission(ClientModel, scope)` looks up the client-specific resource and, when one exists, evaluates only that resource. It never evaluates the all-clients `Clients` resource in that case. A client-specific resource is created whenever any client-specific permission exists for that client, even if it belongs to a different admin. As a result, a user with global `manage`/`configure`/`view` on all clients can be denied access to a client merely because some unrelated client-specific permission exists for it; global deny policies can be bypassed in the same way. The evaluator must combine applicable permissions from both the per-client resource and the all-clients resource rather than treating the per-client resource as a complete replacement.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission cannot see per-client resources
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, but per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` are created with `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` and never assigned type `Clients`; only the all-clients resource created in `init` has that type. Consequently, when only per-client grants exist this method returns an empty set, and when an all-clients grant exists it adds the literal name `Clients` instead of actual client IDs. Callers that use the returned set to filter clients by per-client permission will see incorrect results. Either set the resource type when creating per-client resources or query them in another way.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resources
findings.body: `getResourceName` resolves `Users` resources to usernames and maps the all-users resource to "All users", but the schema now also defines `Clients` and this method has no corresponding branch. Client-specific resources are named with the internal client ID and the all-clients resource is named `Clients`, so permission listings fall back to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null or an internal ID instead of the client ID or "All clients". Add client resolution analogous to the existing user handling.

findings.title: Client deletion no longer cleans up permissions when only V2 is enabled
findings.body: The listener now wraps all cleanup in `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (the V1 feature). With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled and V1 disabled, the `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` branch is skipped, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` anyway, so there is no V2 cleanup path. Per-client resources and scope permissions created for `Clients` survive after their client is deleted, leaving stale authorization data in the admin-permissions client. A V2-specific cleanup path is needed for removed clients.
